Rashi on Niddah 44b:10:1.hebrew: ומטמאה את בועלה - אם היא נדה. אבל פחות מכן, אע"ג שמטמאה במגע, אינה מטמאה את בועלה משום בועל נדה לטומאת ז', אלא משום נוגע ולטומאת ערב:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:10:1.english: And she imparts impurity to the one who has intercourse with her - If she is a nidda. But less than this [age], even though she imparts impurity through contact, she does not impart impurity to the one who has intercourse with her as one who has intercourse with a nidda, for seven-day impurity, but rather as one who touches [her], and for impurity until the evening.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:10:2.english: Lower - [The lower bedding] of one who has intercourse with a menstruating woman.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:1.hebrew: מן הפסולין - כגון חלל, נתין, וממזר, ועבד, ועובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:1.english: Of the disqualified - Such as a ḥalal, a natin, a mamzer, a slave, and an idolater.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:2.hebrew: פסלה - מתרומת אביה, אם היא בת כהן, כדתניא בגמרא דאלמנה לכהן גדול ביבמות (דף סח.): מנין לכהנת, לויה וישראלית שבא עליהן כו'? ת"ל: כי תהיה לאיש זר — כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה, פסלה:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:2.english: He disqualifies her - From her father's terumah, if she is the daughter of a priest, as is taught in the Gemara of [the chapter] "A Widow to a High Priest" in Yevamot (page 68a): "From where [is it derived] regarding a priestess, a Levite woman, and an Israelite woman with whom [an unfit man] engaged in intercourse, etc.? The verse states: 'If she be [married] to an outsider' — once she has engaged in intercourse with [a man who is] unfit for her, he disqualifies her."

Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:3.english: Of all the forbidden relations - Such as her father or her father-in-law.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:4.hebrew: והיא פטורה - מפני שהיא קטנה, ולאו בת עונשין:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:11:4.english: And she is exempt - Because she is a minor, and is not subject to punishment.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:13:1.hebrew: ערב ראש השנה - של שנה רביעית. לרבי מאיר גופיה לא הוי בת ביאה עד יום אחרון של שלישית, דהוא ערב ראש השנה; ולרבנן עד למחר, דמיקלע יום ראשון ברביעית:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:13:1.english: The eve of the New Year - Of the fourth year. According to Rabbi Meir himself, she is not fit for intercourse until the last day of the third [year], which is the eve of the New Year; and according to the Rabbis, until the next day, which falls out as the first day of the fourth [year].

Rashi on Niddah 44b:14:1.hebrew: שלשים יום איכא בינייהו - לרבי מאיר, מכי איקלע שלשים יום בשנה שלישית הויא בת ביאה; ולרבנן, עד דמיקלע שנה רביעית. ואיכא בינייהו טובא:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:14:1.english: Thirty days is [the difference] between them - According to Rabbi Meir, once thirty days have arrived in the third year, she is eligible for intercourse; and according to the Rabbis, [not] until the fourth year arrives. And there is a great [difference] between them.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:1:1.english: In the grave - Because he died before her.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:2:1.english: And it convulsed - A fetus in its mother's womb [convulsed] after her death three convulsions. This shows that she died first.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:3:1.hebrew: לומר שממעט כו' - מתניתין דקתני נוחל ומנחיל, לומר שממעט בחלק בכורה. כגון אם היה בן יום אחד כשמת אביו, והיה לו אח בכור ואח פשוט, ומת הוא אחר אביו - נוחל הוא מאביו את חלק רביעי שבנכסיו, ומנחילו לשני אחיו, וחולקין הבכור והפשוט את חלקו של זה בשוה, ונמצא ממעט בחלק הבכור. דאי לאו איהו, הוה שקיל בכור תרי תילתי, כגון מששה זהובים - ארבעה, ופשוט נוטל ב' זהובים; ועכשיו נוטל הבכור ג' זהובים כנגד שני אחין, ומחלקו של זה - ג' רבעי זהוב, נמצאו ביד בכור ד' זהובים חסר רביע, וביד פשוט ב' זהובים ורביע. ודוקא בן יום א', אבל עובר אינו ממעט, כדאמר לקמן: בן שנולד לאחר מיתת אביו אינו ממעט בחלק הבכורה, ונוטל הבכור שליש בכורתו, ובין שלשתן יחלקו ב' שלישים:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:3:1.english: To say that he reduces, etc. - The mishna, which teaches [that an infant] inherits and bequeaths, [comes] to say that he reduces the portion of the firstborn. For example, if he was one day old when his father died, and he had a firstborn brother and an ordinary brother, and he [the infant] died after his father: he inherits from his father a fourth portion of his estate and bequeaths it to his two brothers, and the firstborn and the ordinary [brother] divide this one's portion equally, and thus it turns out that he reduces the firstborn's portion. For were it not for him, the firstborn would have taken two-thirds — for example, four out of six gold dinars — and the ordinary [brother] would take two gold dinars; but now, the firstborn takes three gold dinars as against two brothers, and from this one's portion [he takes] three-quarters of a gold dinar — it turns out that in the hands of the firstborn are four gold dinars minus a quarter, and in the hands of the ordinary [brother], two gold dinars and a quarter. And [this applies] specifically to [a child] one day old, but a fetus does not reduce [the portion], as [the Gemara] states below: A son who was born after the death of his father does not reduce the portion of the firstborn, and the firstborn takes one-third [of the estate as] his firstborn share, and among the three of them they divide the [remaining] two-thirds.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:3:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא - אמרינן בן יום אחד דממעט, אבל עובר לא:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:3:2.english: What is the reason - [That] we say a one-day-old [child] reduces [the portion of the firstborn], but a fetus does not?

Rashi on Niddah 44b:3:3.english: "And they bore him" we require - This implies during his lifetime.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:4:1.hebrew: בכור שנולד אחר מיתת אביו - כגון מת אביו והאשה מעוברת תאומים, אין היוצא ראשון נוטל פי שנים. בלאו תאומים לא משכחת לה, דכיון דבכור לא נולד עד מות אביו, פשוט מהיכן בא? אי נמי, שהניח ב' נשים מעוברות:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:4:1.english: A firstborn who was born after his father's death - For example, where his father died and the wife was pregnant with twins, the one who emerges first does not receive a double portion. Without twins, you cannot find [such a case], for since the firstborn was not born until the death of his father, from where would an ordinary [son] come? Alternatively, [it is a case] where he left two pregnant wives.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:8:1.hebrew: כמאן דלא כר' שמעון - אכולה מתני' קאי, דקא חשיב בן יום אחד בן קיימא:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:8:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion? It is] not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - This refers to the entire mishna, which considers a one-day-old [child] to be viable.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:8:2.english: In a human - For whereas in an animal, [after] eight days it is not a non-viable newborn.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:1.english: A girl of three years - Intercourse with her is [considered] intercourse in all respects.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:2.english: Is betrothed - If her father handed her over for this.

Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:3.hebrew: אם בא עליה יבם קנאה - וזכה בנכסי אחיו, ליורשה ולטמא לה:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:3.english: If a yavam engages in intercourse with her, he acquires her - And he acquires his brother's property, [and acquires her] to inherit from her and to become ritually impure for her [if he is a priest].

Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:4.hebrew: וחייבין עליה - אם קבל בה אביה קדושין מזה, ובא אחר עליה, נהרג, דביאתה ביאה:
Rashi on Niddah 44b:9:4.english: And one is liable on her account - If her father accepted betrothal on her behalf from this [man], and another [man] engaged in intercourse with her, he is executed, for intercourse with her is [considered] intercourse.

Tosafot on Niddah 44b:14:1.hebrew: שלשים יום איכא בינייהו - הא דלא קאמר יום אחד בשנה חשוב שנה איכא בינייהו, דלרבי מאיר בב' שנים ויום אחד סגי, ולא הוי פליג אברייתא דבסמוך — היינו משום דשנת ג' בשביל יום אחד לא הוה קרי ליה שלש שנים. וא"ת: ולימא דיום ראשון של שנה רביעית איכא בינייהו, דלרבי מאיר במקצת היום סגי, ולרבנן בעינן מעת לעת עד שעה שנולדה, כדאמר פ"ב דזבחים (דף כה:) דשעות פוסלות בקדשים? וי"ל, דקים ליה דרבנן לא בעו מעת לעת. ועוד, דאם כן, אף לר' מאיר הוה ליה למתני ג' שנים ויום אחד, והוה ליה לפרושי דלא בעינן מעת לעת. והא דתנן בפרק אלו נערות (כתובות דף כט.): הגיורת שנתגיירה פחותה מבת ג' שנים ויום אחד יש לה קנס — לא אתיא כרבי מאיר, מדמצריך יום אחד אחר שלש שנים. ואם תאמר: והיכי מוכח התם דרישא כרבי מאיר, דקאמר פרק אלו נערות נערה אין קטנה לא? והתם ע"כ אסיפא דמתני' סמיך, דקתני כל מקום שיש מכר אין קנס, דמנערות איכא למימר דלא אתי למעוטי קטנות אלא בוגרות, דבפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף סו:) תנן: אין חייב הבא על נערה המאורסה עד שתהא נערה, ודייק התם דאתא לאפוקי קטנה, דאי לאפוקי בוגרת, אלא על נערה מבעי ליה, אלמא נערה אפילו קטנה משמע; אלא אסיפא סמיך כדפרישית. והיכי דייק מסיפא דמתני' דרישא נמי ר"מ, כיון דמציעתא לא אתיא כוותיה? וי"ל, דלאו ממש ר"מ היא קאמר, אלא דדייק דתנא דההוא פירקא סבר דקטנה אין לה קנס כדקתני בסיפא, וא"כ נערות נקט לאפוקי קטנות. ורבא דפריך בפ"ק דכתובות (דף יא.): הגיורת יש לה קנס, יהבינן לה קנס דאזלה ואכלה בהיותה נכרית?! אלמא סבר דמתני' סבר דקטנה יש לה קנס — היינו משום דסבר: כיון דהך בבא דגיורת לא אתיא כר' מאיר במאי דנקט שלש שנים ויום אחד, אם כן גם לענין דקטנה יש לה קנס אתיא כרבנן. וה"ה דפריך בפ' ד' וה' (ב"ק לח:) ממתני' דאלו נערות (דף כט.) דקתני כותית יש לה קנס לרבי מאיר — אע"ג דההיא דגיורת לא אתיא כר"מ, מ"מ כיון דסתם מתני' ר"מ היא, מאי דמצינן לאוקומי כוותיה מוקמינן:
Tosafot on Niddah 44b:14:1.english: There is [a difference of] thirty days between them - The reason [Rabbi Yoḥanan] did not say that the difference between them is [whether] one day in a year is considered [equivalent to] a year—such that according to Rabbi Meir two years and one day would suffice, and [Rabbi Yoḥanan] would not be disagreeing with the neighboring baraita—is because on account of [only] one day [into] the third year, [the baraita] would not have called her [a girl of] "three years." And if you say: Then let [Rabbi Yoḥanan] say that the difference between them is [regarding] the first day of the fourth year, [namely,] that according to Rabbi Meir part of the day suffices, whereas according to the Rabbis we require a full twenty-four-hour period (me'et le'et) until the [exact] hour she was born, as it says in the second chapter of Zevachim (25b) that hours disqualify in sacrificial matters? And one can answer: [First,] it was clear to him that the Rabbis do not require a twenty-four-hour period [for human age]. And furthermore, if so, even according to Rabbi Meir [the baraita] should have taught "three years and one day," and should have specified that we do not require a twenty-four-hour period. And that which we learned in a mishna in the chapter Ellu Na'arot (Ketubot 29a): "A female convert who converted [when she was] less than three years and one day old has a fine"—this does not follow Rabbi Meir, since it requires one day after three years. And if you say: But how is it proven there that the opening clause [of that mishna] follows Rabbi Meir, where [the Gemara] says in the chapter Ellu Na'arot: "[For] a young woman (na'arah), yes; [for] a minor (ketannah), no"? And there, perforce, [the Gemara] relied on the closing clause of the mishna, which teaches: "Wherever there is sale, there is no fine"; for from [the word] na'arot [alone], one could say that it did not come to exclude minors, but rather grown women (bogerot). For in the chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 66b), we learned: "One who engages in intercourse with a betrothed young woman is not liable until she is a young woman (na'arah)," and [the Gemara] infers there that this came to exclude a minor, because if it were to exclude a grown woman, it should have stated "only for a young woman," which proves that [the word] na'arah [by itself] can mean even a minor! Rather, [the Gemara] relied on the closing clause, as I explained. But how could it infer from the closing clause of the mishna that the opening clause is also Rabbi Meir, given that the middle clause does not follow him? And one can answer: [The Gemara] did not mean that it is literally [and entirely] Rabbi Meir; rather, it inferred that the Tanna of that chapter holds that a minor does not have a fine, as he taught in the closing clause, and if so, he stated na'arot to exclude minors. And [as for] Rava, who challenged in the first chapter of Ketubot (11a): "[Does] a female convert have a fine?! Do we give her a fine so that she can go and consume [it] while being a gentile?!"—from which it is evident that he held that the mishna maintains that a minor does have a fine—this was because he reasoned: Since this clause of the female convert does not follow Rabbi Meir in that it taught "three years and one day," if so, also with regard to [the rule] that a minor has a fine, it follows the Rabbis. And the same applies to that which [the Gemara] challenged in the chapter Arba'ah ve-Ḥamishah (Bava Kamma 38b) from the mishna of Ellu Na'arot (29a), which taught that a Samaritan woman has a fine, [objecting] against Rabbi Meir: even though that [clause] of the female convert does not follow Rabbi Meir, nevertheless, since an anonymous mishna is [ordinarily attributed to] Rabbi Meir, whatever we can establish according to him, we establish [according to him].

Tosafot on Niddah 44b:3:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא וילדו לו בעינן - למ"ד המזכה לעובר לא קנה, לא איצטריך למדרש מוילדו, כדאמר בפ' מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמב:):
Tosafot on Niddah 44b:3:1.english: What is the reason? We require "and they bore him" - According to the one who holds [that] one who transfers [ownership] to a fetus, [the fetus] does not acquire [it], it was not necessary to derive [this] from "and they bore [him]", as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "Mi SheMet" (Bava Batra 142b).

Tosafot on Niddah 44b:6:1.hebrew: איש כי יכה כל נפש אפילו כל דהו - האי קרא כתיב באמור אל הכהנים. ותימה, דבריש הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פד:) דריש מקרא אחרינא, דכתיב באלה מסעי: כל מכה נפש:
Tosafot on Niddah 44b:6:1.english: [A] man who strikes any soul — even of any degree - This verse is written in [Parashat] Emor El HaKohanim. And it is puzzling, for at the beginning of [chapter] HaNechnakin (Sanhedrin 84b), it expounds another verse, which is written in [Parashat] Eleh Masei: "Whoever strikes a soul."

Tosafot on Niddah 44b:8:1.hebrew: הא לא שהה ספקא הוי - משמע הכא דלרבנן הוי טפי בר קיימא מלרשב"ג, דאפילו בן יום א' הוי לדידהו בן קיימא; וכן בפ' החולץ (יבמות דף לו:). ואילו בתוספתא מתניא פלוגתייהו על בן ח', דלרבנן אפילו שהה שלשים יום הוי נפל, ואתא רשב"ג למימר דאם שהה ל' יום הוי בר קיימא, דאמר בן ז' הוא ואישתהויי אשתהי; וכן בפרק הערל (יבמות דף פ:). ויש לומר דבתרתי פליגי; ודייק מדלא קאמר רשב"ג אם שהה ל' יום אינו נפל, כיון דקאי ארבנן דאמרי בבר ח' דהוי נפל, ומדנקט כל ששהה, משמע דבכל ולדות בעי רשב"ג יום ל'; ואם כן, שמעינהו לרבנן דלאו בל' תלוי, אלא בחדשי ההריון:
Tosafot on Niddah 44b:8:1.english: But [if] it did not survive, it is of uncertain status - It is implied here that according to the Rabbis, [a child] is more [readily considered] viable than according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, for even a one-day-old is viable according to them; and so too in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36b). Whereas in the Tosefta, their dispute is taught regarding an eight-month [child], for according to the Rabbis, even if it survived thirty days it is a non-viable newborn (nefel), and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say that if it survived thirty days it is viable, for we say: It is a seven-month [child] whose birth was delayed; and so [it is taught] in the chapter [entitled] HeArel (Yevamot 80b). And one can say that they dispute concerning two [matters]; and [the Gemara] infers [this] from the fact that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel did not say, "If it survived thirty days it is not a non-viable newborn" — since he was addressing the Rabbis who say regarding an eight-month [child] that it is a non-viable newborn — and from the fact that he formulated [it as], "Any [child] that survived," this implies that with regard to all newborns Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel requires thirty days; and if so, we can deduce regarding the Rabbis that [viability] does not depend on thirty [days], but rather on the months of pregnancy.

Tosafot on Niddah 44b:8:2.hebrew: דקים ליה דכלו לו חדשיו - הא לא קים ליה, ספקא הוי. ובנפל מן הגג או אכלו ארי איירי, דבפיהק ומת, אפילו לרבנן הוי נפל, כדאמר פרק רבי אליעזר אם לא הביא (שבת קלו.). ואם תאמר: אם כן, מאי טעמא דרשב"ג? כיון דליכא ריעותא, אמאי אינו מתאבל עליו, דניזיל אחר רוב ולדות דהוו בני קיימא? ובפ' רבי אליעזר אם לא הביא (שם), דאסר ההוא עגלה דאשתחיט ביומא דשביעאה משום דהתם פסיק הלכה כרשב"ג — אמאי לא אזלינן בתר רובא? וי"ל, דנפלין הוי מיעוט דשכיח, ודבר ההווה הוא, ולכך החמירו חכמים, ולענין אבלות הקילו. וגדולה מזאת מצינו, דאמר בפרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מט.): דיום ל' כשלפניו לענין אבלות, אע"ג דקי"ל בהחולץ (יבמות לו:) דמת ביום ל' ועמדה ונתקדשה, אם אשת כהן היא אינה חולצת, דחשיב בר קיימא. וא"ת: דהכא אמר דבלא שהה ספקא הוא ואינו מתאבל עליו, ובמסכת שמחות (פ"ד ה"ב) תנן: ספק אחיו ספק אינו אחיו מתאבל עליו? וי"ל, דשאני התם, כיון דבר קיימא הוא, אי אין מתאבל עליו סברי עלמא דאין מתאבלין על אחין. א"נ, בספק בן ט' לראשון או בן ז' לאחרון, דמה נפשך חד מינייהו חייב, וגנאי הדבר לפטור שניהם:
Tosafot on Niddah 44b:8:2.english: Where it is established for him that its months were completed - Whereas if it is not established for him [that its months were completed], it is [a case of] doubt. And we are dealing with [a case where] it fell from the roof or a lion ate it, for if it yawned and died, even according to the Rabbis it is [considered] a non-viable newborn (nefel), as it says in the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer Im Lo Hevi" (Shabbat 136a). And if you say: If so, what is the reasoning of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel? Since there is no apparent defect, why does one not mourn for him, for let us follow the majority of newborns, who are viable? And in the chapter "Rabbi Eliezer Im Lo Hevi" (ibid.), where [Shmuel] prohibited that calf which was slaughtered on the seventh day because there [the Gemara] ruled the halakhah in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel — why do we not follow the majority? And one can say: Non-viable births (nefelin) are a frequent minority and a common occurrence, and therefore the Sages were stringent [regarding prohibitions], and regarding mourning they were lenient. And greater than this we have found, as it says in the chapter "Yesh Bekhor" (Bekhorot 49a): The thirtieth day is like [the days] before it regarding mourning, even though we hold in [the chapter] "HaCholetz" (Yevamot 36b) that if [the child] died on the thirtieth day and she went and became betrothed, if she is the wife of a priest she does not perform chalitzah, because he is considered a viable child. And if you say: Here [the Gemara] says that if he did not survive [thirty days], it is [a case of] doubt and one does not mourn for him; yet in Tractate Semachot (4:2) we learned: [If one is in] doubt [whether the deceased was] his brother or not his brother, he mourns for him? And one can say: It is different there, since he was a viable person; if he does not mourn for him, people will think that one does not mourn for brothers. Alternatively, [it refers to] an uncertain case of a nine-month [child] of the first [husband] or a seven-month [child] of the latter [husband], so that in any event (mah nafshekh) one of them is obligated, and it would be disgraceful to exempt both of them.
